From my perspective as Brandon:

At the lunch meeting, I was uneasy. I worried that Benjamin might see my cautious, detail-heavy style as boring or overly technical. When Benjamin responded positively, laughed, and said he actually appreciated both my thoroughness and the lighter moments, it changed how I believed he perceived me. I no longer felt like I had to protect against being seen as too dry or too cautious. His positive reception gave me confidence that the rapport was strong enough to go beyond transactional insurance advice. That is why, by the next scenario, I felt pleased and wanted to strengthen the professional relationship by offering additional value. The shift came from Benjamin’s positive response to my personal anecdote and engagement, not from a formal partnership idea, which I had not yet proposed.
